proof_attempt_summary: Derived and independently audited the signed learned-fit quadratic transition, uniform same-data observable calibration over all deterministic repeat budgets, and critical/subcritical local-power laws for the fixed finite-stratum saturated IFSS model. The mathematics passed D0.5 and all five cited claims were verified against lawful source statements, but the delivered package achieved incremental significance below the field floor. Formalization was not started; the zero-variance boundary requires a new model and research program.
tldr: For the exact repeated Yu intra-fold CATE-variance point statistic, with the same saturated training fits reused across reallocations, the note proves an original-record quadratic plus allocation-noise decomposition and its uniform reference law at scale \(a_{nB}=\sqrt{n^{-2}+(nB)^{-1}}\). The transition occurs at \(B\asymp n\): allocation noise dominates below this order, while the signed learned-CATE quadratic term remains at and above it, including \(B/n\to\infty\). A fully observable Gaussian-polynomial simulator using the same records gives asymptotic null size \(.05\), uniformly over the complete stated compact null \(\mathcal P_0\) and every deterministic integer \(1\le B\le n^2\). The calibrated test has strict directional root-\(n\) local power at critical and supercritical budgets and CATE sensitivity scale \((nB)^{-1/4}\) for \(B=o(n)\). For each fixed nonzero legal interior direction, strict asymptotic excess over size for arbitrary deterministic budget sequences holds precisely when \(\liminf_n B_n/n>0\). These conclusions concern this procedure in a fixed finite-stratum, binary-outcome, compact-interior, saturated-count model, a strict specialization of Yu's broader class.
